text:
LLM Hub

 

 LLM Hub is an open-source app for on-device LLM chat, image generation, video generation, and music generation, available for both Android and iOS , and now on Windows , macOS and Linux as LLM Hub Desktop. It's optimized for mobile usage (CPU/GPU/NPU acceleration) and supports multiple model formats so you can run powerful models locally and privately.

 Featured: Featured by RunAnywhere on their website. Read the LLM Hub iOS Case Study!

 Download

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 LLM Hub Desktop

 LLM Hub Desktop 0.1.3 is out: native apps for Windows, macOS and Linux. Chat with local models, run Claude Code and OpenClaw on them, turn prompts into slides and pages, generate images, video and music, and serve OpenAI and Anthropic compatible APIs to your other apps. No account and no cloud. See the release notes for what's new and checksums.

 Download For 
 --- --- 
 macOS Mac with Apple silicon, macOS 26 or later. Signed and notarized. 
 Windows x64 Windows 10 (version 2004) or later on an Intel or AMD PC 
 Windows on Arm Snapdragon PCs 
 Linux .deb Ubuntu 24.04 or later, Debian and their derivatives 
 Linux AppImage Other x64 distributions with GTK 4 and libadwaita 1.4 or later 

The Windows installers aren't code signed yet, so Windows may show "Windows protected your PC": click More info , then Run anyway . Signing is being set up, see the code signing policy. To build it yourself, see desktop/README.md.

 Code signing policy

Free code signing provided by SignPath.io, certificate by SignPath Foundation.

- Signed Windows builds are built only from this repository's source, by the Desktop Windows installers workflow on GitHub-hosted runners.
- Committers and reviewers: Timmy Qian
- Approvers: Timmy Qian, who approves every signing request in SignPath
- Privacy: see the LLM Hub privacy policy

 Features

 AI Tools Suite
 Tool Description 
 ------ ------------- 
 Chat Multi-turn conversations with RAG memory, web search, TTS auto-readout, and multimodal input 
 AI Agent Autonomous device agent with function calling, interactive maps, device tools, MCP tools, and Termux terminal command generation on Android 
 creAItor Design custom AI personas with specialized system prompts (PCTF) in seconds 
 Vibe Coder Build apps with live HTML/JS preview; Android also runs Codex and Claude Code through Termux using your selected local model 
 Writing Aid Summarize, expand, rewrite, improve grammar, or generate code from descriptions 
 Image Generator Create images from text prompts using Stable Diffusion 1.5 with swipeable gallery 
 Music Generator Generate music and sound effects locally with Stable Audio 3 (Small Music, Small SFX, Medium) and SoundGen on Android, and Magenta Realtime 2 on iOS and Snapdragon Android, with live playback as music is generated (iOS, and Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5/Gen 6) 
 Instant Media Search Search photos and videos by description or a reference image on Android and iOS using on-device EmbeddingGemma 2 
 Video Moment Finder Describe a moment in a video and jump to matching timestamps using visual and audio embeddings on Android and iOS 
 Text to Speech & Voice Cloning Android supports Kokoro, multilingual Supertonic 3 with voice-profile import, Pocket TTS with on-device voice cloning, and Phonon 
 Image Upscale Upscale images up to 4× using AI super-resolution models (RealESRGAN, UltraSharp) with NPU acceleration 
 Object Eraser Paint over objects to remove them from photos on Android, with MI-GAN (Quick) or LaMa (HD) on the GPU with CPU fallback 
 Video Generator Generate videos from text prompts or images: LTX-Video on Android (Snapdragon NPU, Vulkan GPU or CPU), Stable Video Diffusion on iOS 
 Translator Translate text, images (OCR), and audio across 50+ languages - offline 
 Transcriber Convert speech to text on-device with Whisper, Moonshine, Parakeet, ML Kit or audio-capable Gemma models 
 Scam Detector Analyze messages and images for phishing with risk assessment 
 VibeVoice Hands-free AI voice chat 

 AI Agent & Termux Terminal Command Generation
The AI Agent turns on-device LLMs into autonomous assistants with device function calling capabilities:
- Device Actions & Function Calling : Embedded interactive maps (OpenStreetMap), calendar management, alarm setup, flashlight toggle, SMS & Email composition, cryptographic hashing (SHA-256/MD5), and math calculation.
- MCP Tools : Connect Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers so the Agent can discover and use external tools such as filesystem, search, document, memory, or custom hosted tools. MCP calls require user approval before execution.
- Termux Command Generation (Android) : Automatically drafts shell/CLI commands targeting Termux environment execution ( RUN COMMAND SERVICE intent interface).
- Interactive Pre-Execution Editing : Users can inspect and edit AI-generated shell commands before execution.
- Live Dark Terminal Container : Formats and streams live command outputs ( stdout / stderr ) in a dark monospace terminal UI block.
- AI Error Auto-Correction Loop : When a shell command fails or encounters permission/syntax errors, the agent automatically feeds the error logs back into the LLM for self-diagnostics and auto-generates fix commands.

 Supported ASR Models (Android)
The offline Transcriber on Android works with dedicated speech recognition models and with chat models that take audio input:
- Whisper Tiny and Base (English-only and multilingual) through WhisperKit on LiteRT, with Qualcomm NPU acceleration on supported Snapdragon chips.
- Whisper Tiny int8 in Goog

AI Agent & Termux Terminal Command Generation

The AI Agent turns on-device LLMs into autonomous assistants with device function calling capabilities:

  • Device Actions & Function Calling: Embedded interactive maps (OpenStreetMap), calendar management, alarm setup, flashlight toggle, SMS & Email composition, cryptographic hashing (SHA-256/MD5), and math calculation.
  • MCP Tools: Connect Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers so the Agent can discover and use external tools such as filesystem, search, document, memory, or custom hosted tools. MCP calls require user approval before execution.
  • Termux Command Generation (Android): Automatically drafts shell/CLI commands targeting Termux environment execution (RUN_COMMAND_SERVICE intent interface).
  • Interactive Pre-Execution Editing: Users can inspect and edit AI-generated shell commands before execution.
  • Live Dark Terminal Container: Formats and streams live command outputs (stdout/stderr) in a dark monospace terminal UI block.
  • AI Error Auto-Correction Loop: When a shell command fails or encounters permission/syntax errors, the agent automatically feeds the error logs back into the LLM for self-diagnostics and auto-generates fix commands.
Supported ASR Models (Android)

The offline Transcriber on Android works with dedicated speech recognition models and with chat models that take audio input:

  • Whisper Tiny and Base (English-only and multilingual) through WhisperKit on LiteRT, with Qualcomm NPU acceleration on supported Snapdragon chips.
  • Whisper Tiny int8 in Google's LiteRT-LM format (~42 MB): fast English transcription on CPU or GPU.
  • Moonshine Tiny (~30 MB): the fastest and lightest English model, on CPU.
  • Whisper ACFT Tiny, Base and Small (English, ~60 to 287 MB): FUTO's Whisper fine-tuned for 10-second windows, so short recordings are not padded to 30 seconds.
  • NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3: 25 European languages with automatic language detection. A LiteRT-LM build runs on any device; NPU builds run on Snapdragon 8 Gen 2, 8 Gen 3, 8 Elite and 8 Elite Gen 5, Google Tensor G5 and G6, and MediaTek Dimensity 9400 and 9500.
  • Google ML Kit speech recognition (Basic, and Advanced on recent flagships): the system installs and updates the model, so it uses no app storage.
  • Gemma-3n and Gemma-4 (E2B and E4B): multimodal models with audio input can transcribe too.
Android Text to Speech & Voice Cloning
  • Kokoro: Local speech with downloadable voices managed in Settings.
  • Supertonic 3: Multilingual on-device speech with downloadable presets and import of compatible voice-style JSON files. Raw audio cloning and Pocket TTS voice states are not supported by Supertonic's importer. See Supertonic 3 setup.
  • Phonon 31M: Small, fast English speech (~84 MB) with five built-in voices.
  • Pocket TTS: English speech and fully local voice cloning from recorded or imported audio. Manage, select, rename and delete cloned voices in Settings. Cloning uses 3 to 30 seconds of reference audio; longer imports use their first 30 seconds. See Pocket TTS setup.
  • Selecting an engine and voice in Settings applies it to app-wide speech and auto-readout. Translator keeps system TTS.
Media Search & Video Moment Finder

On Android and iOS, Instant Media Search uses EmbeddingGemma 2 to index photos and videos locally, then find matches from a text description or reference image. Video Moment Finder combines video frames and audio from two-second windows so you can search for a scene or event and play the matching moment. Download a compatible EmbeddingGemma 2 model and choose the media to index; search runs on-device.

Android Vibe Coder, Codex & Claude Code

Enable Codex mode in Vibe Coder's model settings to use the selected on-device model with the Codex app server running in Termux. Codex can inspect project files, edit code and run project commands, with streamed activity and terminal output in the app. This mode requires an ARM64 device running Android 10 or newer and does not require an OpenAI login. Install Termux, allow external app commands, grant LLM Hub permission to run Termux commands, and use the in-app Install Codex action before starting.

Enable Claude Code mode in the same settings to run Claude Code in Termux on the selected on-device model instead. It reads and edits project files and runs commands the same way, and does not require an Anthropic account. The requirements and Termux setup are the same; use the in-app Install Claude Code in Termux action before starting. Only one of the two modes can be on at a time.

Android Video Generation

The Android Video Generator runs Lightricks LTX-Video 2B 0.9.8 distilled fully on-device, from a text prompt or a starting image, in 8 denoising steps.

  • Snapdragon NPU: The transformer and VAE decoder run on the Hexagon NPU as QNN context binaries, one build per Hexagon generation: v69 (8 Gen 1, 8+ Gen 1), v73 (8 Gen 2), v75 (8 Gen 3), v79 (8 Elite), v81 (8 Elite Gen 5) and v85 (8 Elite Gen 6), plus an integer-only v73 build for chips whose NPU has no FP16 (8s Gen 4, 8s Gen 3, 7+ Gen 3, 7 Gen 4). A 25-frame 768x512 clip takes about 25 seconds on a Snapdragon 8 Elite; v69 and v73 chips generate at 512x320. Models: timmyboy26/LTX-Video-2B-0.9.8-distilled-QNN.
  • Other chips: GGUF models (Q4_0 / Q8_0) run through stable-diffusion.cpp with Vulkan on the GPU, or on the CPU. A 25-frame 512x320 clip takes about 3 minutes on an Exynos 1580 (Galaxy A56) and about 20 minutes on a Tensor G3 (Pixel 8 Pro).
  • Open Video Generator, download a model from the Video Generation tab, and choose the model and backend in the settings sheet. Detailed prompts that describe the subject, action, camera and lighting work best.
  • The scripts that build the NPU models are in android/tools/ltxv_qnn.
iOS Live Music Generation

The iOS Music Generator supports Live generation with Magenta Realtime 2: hear audio as it is generated while the app writes it to a local file. Enable Unlimited duration to keep generating until you press Stop, or use a fixed duration. Fixed-duration output uses WAV; unlimited sessions use CAF for long recordings.

Privacy First
